title: France – Electricity transmission pylons – Fourniture de liaisons de dépannage 400 kV(Emergency Restoring System)
description: Le marché envisagé a pour objet la fourniture de liaisons de dépannage, pouvant notamment être mises en oeuvre dans l’hypothèse d’évènements climatiques extrêmes entrainant des avaries sur le réseau électrique. 2 liaisons seront livrées dans le cadre du marché envisagé (en 2027). Il est prévu de solliciter la fourniture de modules et accessoires permettant l’installation de lignes de secours aériennes constituées de mâts haubanés d’une longueur totale de 2,5 kilomètres en faisceau double (câble conducteur de section 570 mm2) pour chaque liaison, chaque portée ayant une longueur minimale de 250 mètres. De manière accessoire, les matériels livrés doivent permettre la mise en œuvre de configurations de lignes différentes (lignes de longueur moindre, avec un nombre de mâts d’ancrage/de suspension différent). RTE a également identifié que l’amont industriel est en mesure de proposer des matériels permettant l’installation de lignes de secours en faisceau triple. Aussi, il est envisagé de solliciter auprès des fournisseurs invités à participer à la consultation la remise de propositions portant sur cette solution. Il convient de noter que les prestations envisagées n’ont pas pour objet la fourniture de câbles conducteurs et d’entretoises.

title: Chemical Nutrient Analysis Service
description: The U.S. Army Contracting Command � Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG), Natick Division, in support of the U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command � Soldier Center (DEVCOM-SC), Soldier Sustainment Directorate (SSD) / Combat Feeding Division (CFD) located in Natick, MA 01760, has a requirement for nutrient analysis services for the U.S. Army Combat Feeding Division. The Combat Feeding Division�s Nutrient Analysis Laboratory (NAL) currently has multiple samples to analyze for nutritional content. The CFD, part of the U.S. Army DEVCOM-SC, is the Department of Defense�s centralized source for all research, development, engineering, and integration of joint service combat rations, food service equipment and field feeding systems. CFD�s primary mission is to ensure Warfighters have the tactical, nutritional and logistical advantage required to survive and win on the battlefield. Although CFD already has an in-house Nutrient Analysis Lab (NAL), there is currently a short-term need to outsource select nutrient analysis services for ingredients and ration components. The contractor shall provide laboratory nutrient analysis testing on provided food samples. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercially available services prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Subpart 12.6 as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; proposals are being requested, and a written solicitation will not be issued. Request For Proposal (RFP) number is: W911QY-26-R-CHEMICAL-NUTRIENT-ANALYSIS. The Government intends to award a single, Firm Fixed Price (FFP) contract as a result of this solicitation. All timely offers will be considered, and proposal submission shall be in accordance with Submission Instructions contained herein. Evaluation factors are Technical Capability, Price, and Past Performance. The Government intends to make award to the Offeror whose proposal represents the Best Value to the Government. This requirement is set for full and open competition. This is not set-aside to small businesses. The NAICS code is 541380 - Testing Laboratories and Services. The small business size standard is $19M. The Army�s Office for Small Business Programs concurs with the full and open competition determination. Incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular 2025-01. FAR Clauses 52.212-1 through 52.212-5 and DFARS 52.212-7001, Contract Terms and Conditions Required to Implement Statutes or Executive Orders Applicable to Defense Acquisitions of Commercial Items (see www.acquisition.gov) apply to this procurement. Contractors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) (https://www.sam.gov) to be eligible for award. Instructions for registration are available at the website. Any additional contract requirement(s) or terms and conditions determined by the Contracting Officer to be necessary for this acquisition and consistent with customary commercial practices shall apply. Submission Instructions: All Offerors shall submit a proposal consisting of three (3) sections. These three (3) sections shall be labeled; Section I � Technical Proposal; Section II � Pricing Proposal; and Section III � Past Performance. No Pricing Information shall be submitted in Section I. Evaluation will be in accordance with FAR 52.212-2 Evaluation--Commercial Items and Commercial Services. (a) The Government intends to award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror whose offer conforming to this solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The following factors shall be used to evaluate offers: I. Technical capability of services offered to meet Government requirements: Requirements: The contractor shall be able to analyze samples for the analytes in Table 1 (See Attached Statement of Work for Table 1) with the preferred methods listed below or equivalent* with the listed limits of quantification (LOQ). The main analytes that will be requested are 1) selenium, 2) vitamin B12 (cobalamin) and 3) total dietary fiber. However, the contractor must also have the ability to analyze for any of the other analytes listed below, in case CFD has a need to have those analytes determined as well. This SOW is for an indeterminate quantity of samples (25-100), up to $25K during the period of performance. No more than 25 samples would be sent at one time. Analyses and results shall be completed and delivered to the government no later than 14 calendar days after receipt of samples. Contractor shall prepare a data report for each set of samples that has been analyzed to include sample name/ID, method used, results, units of measure, limit of quantification and date of analysis. *If the contractor proposes to use a different method than the preferred methods listed, than that method must be specified in their proposal as well as the LOQ of that method. If the method is not an industry standard method (publicly available), then please attach a copy of the method in the proposal. During market research the price ranges in Table 2 (See Attached Statement of Work for Table 2) were determined to be reasonable per analyte (dependent on the method proposed). Contractor�s proposals must include the cost/test and the proposed method w/ LOQ. A cost/test can be outside of this range, but the proposals will be evaluated based on the demonstrated ability of the contractor to meet the requirements, proposed methods with LOQ and the cost/test. a. General Requirements In-House Capacity: The contractor must have the in-house capacity (personnel, equipment, etc.) to perform the analyses requested. Contractors acting as pass throughs to larger labs will not be accepted. Accreditation: The contractor shall maintain active ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation for the duration of the contract. The accreditation scope must cover the specific nutritional tests requested. Analytical Methodology: All testing must utilize validated, industry-standard methods (e.g., AOAC International, USP, AACC, or equivalent recognized methods). If an alternative method is used, the contractor must provide scientific validation prior to testing. Sample Custody & Tracking: The contractor must maintain a documented chain of custody from sample receipt at the facility until final disposal. Communication & Support: The contractor shall designate a primary point of contact (POC) or project manager to handle inquiries, clarify test results, and resolve sample receipt issues within 24 hours. Storage Conditions: Upon receipt, the contractor shall store all samples under the conditions specified by the government (e.g., ambient, refrigerated at 4�C, or frozen at -20�C) to prevent nutrient degradation before analysis. Sample Retention: The contractor must retain the remaining homogenized sample material for a minimum of 30 calendar days after the final report is delivered, allowing the government to request re-testing if anomalies are found. Disposal: After the 30-day retention period, the contractor shall safely dispose of the food samples in accordance with local environmental regulations at no additional cost to the government. b. Specific Requirements See Attached Statement of Work for Table containing the Specific Requirements and additional details. II. Price: Reference Table 1 & 2 in the attached SOW. III. Past Performance: Offerors are reminded that while the Government may elect to consider data obtained from other sources, the burden of providing thorough and complete past performance information rests with the Offeror. Offerors shall submit three (3) recent and relevant past performance examples performed within the last three years. Each example shall not exceed two (2) pages and shall include the following: 1. Contract number, date of award, order number if applicable, CAGE code, DUNS number, and North American Industry Classification

title: Maintenance of Satellite Communication System
description: THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT AND IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE QUOTES. Naval Supply Systems Command (NAVSUP) Fleet Logistics Center San Diego (FLCSD) intends to award a commercial, firm fixed price (FFP) contract to the University of Alaska Fairbanks; 2145 N Tanana Loop, Fairbanks, AK 99775. Under the authority of FAR 12.102(a), only one responsible source is reasonably available, and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. The requirement is for the purchase of hosting, maintenance, and technical support necessary to maintain a satellite communication system located at the Alaska Satellite Facility (ASF) in Fairbanks, AK. This is in support of the Mobile CubeSat Command and Control (MC3) ground station network, which is part of a comprehensive system of satellite design, testing and operations in which students participate at the Naval Postgraduate School (NPS). Currently, the MC3 network includes a total of ten antennas located at facilities across the U.S., with one being at ASF in Fairbanks, AK, so maintenance and technical support are needed for the satellite system at the Fairbanks, AK location. For a complete description of all the required services, please review the attached Performance Work Statement (PWS).The anticipated award date of this action is on or before 28 September 2026. The applicable NAICS code is 517810: All Other Telecommunications. This acquisition will follow the simplified procedures in FAR 12.201-1: Simplified procedures. Current market research suggests that the University of Alaska Fairbanks (UAF) is the only contractor capable of fulfilling this requirement due to a combination of unique geographical advantages, physical control of the infrastructure site, proprietary site-access restrictions, and specialized technical expertise. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotations, and no solicitation document exists for the requirement. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement which shall be considered by the agency. Sources interested in responding to this notice are required to submit a capability statement that includes information in sufficient detail and with convincing evidence that clearly demonstrates the capability to provide all required services in the attached Performance Work Statement (PWS). Capability statements shall not exceed 6 (8.5 x 11 inch) pages using a font size no smaller than 10-point. All capability statements received by the due date of this notice will be considered by the Government. A request for documentation or additional information or submissions that only ask questions will not be considered as an affirmative response. A determination by the Government not to compete based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. title: J--Amendment #4 to 1333MF26Q0108
description: Continuation page from block 14. The Amendment 0004 covers the final Q&A / Questions & Answers #2 within the Solicitation No. 1333MF26Q0108 Questions and Answers #2 1333MF26Q0108 (26-509) SEFSC Galveston AC Preventative Maintenance Contract Q1. Contractor licensing. The Statement of Work states that the contractor "must possess a working knowledge of Water Source Heat Pumps, Heat Pumps and Portable AC Units, and be licensed and hold the appropriate certifications in the state of Texas." Please confirm whether the Government requires the quoter/prime contractor to hold a Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Contractor license in its own name, or whether that requirement is satisfied where the licensed contractor and the licensed and EPA-certified technicians performing the work are a subcontractor to the quoter. A: The Personnel on site should have the applicable certifications associated with the project requirements. Q2. Subcontractor past performance. Evaluation Factor 3 requires at least two past performance references and states that a quoter with no relevant past performance must affirmatively say so. Please confirm whether, and how, the Government will consider the past performance and experience of a proposed subcontractor that will perform the technical work, where that subcontractor's references are identified as such. A: Past performance is rated on the prime/vendor proposing. The government does not have visibility of subcontractors. Q3. Limitations on subcontracting. FAR 52.219-6 appears in the clause list; FAR 52.219-14 does not appear expressly, though FAR 52.212-5 is attached. Please confirm that 52.219-14 is incorporated for this total small business set-aside and that the applicable limitation is paragraph (e)(1), 50 percent, for services. A: FAR 52.219-14 is for actions exceeding the Simplified Acquisition Threshold of which this action does not, therefore this clause is not applicable to this action. Based on the foundational principals of small business set aside, by submitting a proposal, the prime contractor is certifying to the federal government that a small business is providing the primary solution. A small business prime contractor cannot legally subcontract most of the work to a large business. Doing so constitutes a serious federal procurement violation known as "pass-through fraud" or acting as a "front." Q4. Filter quantities. Amended Annex A provides filter sizes and locations and Amendment 0002 confirms MERV 10 throughout. Please provide, or confirm, the number of filters per unit per service event and the total filter count per service event, so that all quoters price the same material quantity. A: Correct quantities were provided in the most recent Amendment 0002 Q5. Cleaning frequency. Amendment 0002 states the initial event is a full cleaning of coils, drains and filter changes, and that filters are changed monthly. Please confirm whether the cleaning of coils, condensate pans, drain lines, grilles and cabinets recurs at every monthly event after the initial event, or on a different cycle (quarterly, semi-annual, annual), and confirm how the close-out service differs. A: Initial work will include all tasks (full cleaning of coils, drains and filter change). On a monthly basis the filters will be changed. All other tasks will be performed quarterly. Q6. Exhaust fan belts. The Statement of Work references exhaust fan belts. Please confirm whether belt replacement is within the firm-fixed-price scope, and if so provide the number of belts and their sizes. A: Fan belt for exhaust fans is an A26 belt, there are 9 total. Q7. Site access and escort. Please state the normal hours during which work may be performed, whether contractor personnel require a Government escort in occupied laboratory or office spaces, and the lead time for Real ID verification, sign-in and visitor badging in Building 307 for a recurring monthly crew. A: All personnel will be required to sign in and be escorted into most all areas across the campus. Sign-in and signing-out are mandatory, the requirement for a �Real-ID� is a stipulation in the solicitation, the use of a Passport can be an acceptable form as an alternative. As for lead time, I assume this question is about the lead time required to get the License converted to a Real-ID, per the Texas Department of Safety (aka the DMV) there is a three day lag for appointments here in the Galveston Office. Q8. Access equipment and staging. Please confirm whether any of the designated AHUs, FCUs or water-source units require lift, scaffold or ceiling-tile access rather than a standard ladder, and whether the Government will make interior space available for staging replacement filters on service days. A: 95% of the units, as identified during the site visits, are located under ceiling tiles. Technicians will be required to climb an 8 to 9 foot ladder to access them. On the day of service we can provide a staging area for material on the day of work, but not for long-term storage. Q9. Disposal. Please confirm whether the Government provides on-site waste disposal for removed filters and cleaning debris, or whether the contractor must haul all removed material off site. A: Contractor should remove all waste to include filters and packing materials from the Campus. Debris should not be placed in the Dumpsters on the campus. Q10. Johnson Controls. Amendment 0001 states the contractor "must be familiar with Johnson Controls referencing HVAC specifically." Please clarify the scope of that interaction - whether contractor personnel are expected to operate, silence, reset or otherwise interact with the Johnson Controls building automation system in connection with filter changes and cleaning, or whether familiarity is required only so that contractor work does not conflict with the existing controls. A: Familiarity is required as the contractor will have to understand when the units are running and see the status on the VLx and communication boxes associated with each unit. Q11. Certifications and documentary evidence. The Statement of Work requires, at a minimum, Site Safety and Health Support, Preventive Maintenance Coordination, OSHA Training, Quality Control Management Training, and EM 385-1-1 Safety Familiarity, and Factor 1 requires written documentation of the quoter's certifications. Please identify what documentation satisfies each - certificate copies, training rosters, or a signed statement of compliance - and confirm whether EM 385-1-1 familiarity is required given that EM 385-1-1 is a USACE safety manual. A: Copies of certificates will suffice, I am required to maintain copies on site, as they will be inspectable during Standard Safety and Occupational Health Inspections. Q12. Service Contract Labor Standards. Wage Determination 2015-5233 Rev. 35 is incorporated. Please confirm the labor categories the Government considers applicable to this scope, and confirm whether any incumbent employees are subject to FAR 52.222-17 Nondisplacement of Qualified Workers, and if so provide the seniority list. A: The government deems the following to be applicable 23410 - Heating, Ventilation And Air-Conditioning Mechanic 23411 - Heating, Ventilation And Air Conditioning Mechanic (Research Facility) 23810 - Plumber, Maintenance Q13. Quote format. Please confirm whether there is a page limit, font, or file-format requirement for the quotation, and confirm the Government's preferred method for acknowledging Amendments 0001, 0002 and 0003 - signed SF30s returned with the quote, or acknowledgment by letter. A: The proposals should be no more than 8 pages total for all sections. Signed SF30�s is the preferred format for acknowledging Amendments but acknowledgement by letter within the proposal is acceptable as well.Vendors shall monitor SAM.gov for all future possible amendments as well. title: IDENTIFY Study Participants � 5-Base Sample Preparation and Whole Genome Multiomic Profiling
description: The Prenatal Genomics and Therapy Section (PGTS), Center for Precision Health Research (CPHR), National Human Genome Research Institute (NHGRI), requires 5-base whole genome sequencing services for stored plasma-derived cell-free DNA samples collected under the IDENTIFY study. These samples were obtained from women who received prenatal cell-free DNA sequencing results suggestive of maternal malignancy. 5Base sample prep and whole genome multiomic profiling at 30x is required to generate high-resolution genomic and epigenomic data suitable for tissue-of-origin analyses. The objective of this acquisition is to obtain high-quality, comprehensive 5-base sequencing data that will support the development and refinement of computational models to determine the tissue source of incidentally detected maternal cancers. The resulting data will be incorporated into ongoing bioinformatic and translational research efforts within PGTS to improve interpretation of prenatal cell-free DNA sequencing results, enhance early cancer detection strategies in pregnancy, and advance understanding of circulating cell-free DNA biology in the context of malignancy.

description: Continued... Continuation page from block 14. The purpose of this amendment is to respond to the questions received for Solicitation No. 1333MF26Q0109. Combined Synopsis Solicitation: 1333MF26Q0109 Response to Questions: Q1 - Could you please confirm whether bid, performance, and payment bonds are required for this solicitation? A1 - The winning vendor must be licensed and bonded in the state the work is to be performed. The attached wage determination is for services not construction as we are considering this work to be repairs and maintenance not construction. Q2 - Could you please clarify whether we may use a subcontractor that is licensed and bonded in the State of Florida to satisfy this requirement, or whether the licensing and bonding requirements must be held by the prime contractor?� A2 - The government has no privity with a subcontractor therefore all requirements fall upon the primary contractor. Subcontractors must also be licensed and trained to work in the state. Q3 - The SOW states that vendor teams shall be licensed and bonded to work in Miami, Florida. May the prime contractor satisfy this requirement through its licensed and bonded HVAC subcontractor, or must the prime contractor independently hold the applicable HVAC license and bond? A3 - Please see responses above Q4 - For Evaluation Factors 2 � Experience and 3 � Past Performance, will NOAA consider the relevant experience, qualifications, and past-performance references of the prime contractor�s proposed HVAC subcontractor and key personnel? A4 - Both the prime and any proposed subcontractors should have the relevant past performance and experience working on this type of requirement. Q5 - For Tasks 4 and 5, should offerors price the quotation assuming complete replacement of both systems, or should anticipated repair and full-system replacement be priced separately? A5 - Complete replacement of both systems Q6 - For Task 8, should offerors assume replacement of all identified strainer/check valves for purposes of the firm-fixed-price quotation? If so, can NOAA provide the applicable valve sizes, types, and quantities? A6 - The government does not have documentation of the valve sizes, types, or quantities for these assemblies, and no as-built or submittal data is available. The scope of Task 8 is limited to inspection at the three locations identified and replacement of only those assemblies found leaking or non-operational. For pricing purposes, offerors shall assume one strainer/check valve assembly at each of the three locations, serving fan-coil equipment. Offerors should state any pricing assumptions in their quotation. Any condition materially different from the above will be addressed by the Contracting Officer. Q7 - Please confirm that offerors should provide one firm-fixed price for CLIN 0001 covering the complete 60-day requirement. The combined synopsis references monthly and annual pricing for base and option years, while the SOW appears to establish a single 60-day project requirement. A7 - There is only one CLIN in this action. Verbiage in the invoicing section is standard template language. Q8 - Is Miami-Dade County Notice of Acceptance or equivalent Florida Product Approval required for all replacement HVAC equipment under Tasks 1�5, or only for the Task 3 warehouse system? A8 - Miami-Dade County Notice of Acceptance or equivalent Florida product approval is required for all exterior-mounted replacement equipment, including the Task 1 and Task 2 packaged rooftop units and the outdoor condensing units under Tasks 3, 4, and 5. Indoor air handlers are not subject to this requirement. Q9 - Please confirm whether permits from the local municipality are required for the replacement of the HVAC equipment. A9 - The Miami campus is a federally owned facility. County mechanical permits are not required for work performed on this site. All work shall comply with the applicable standards listed in the SOW, including the National Electrical Code, ASHRAE standards, and Miami-Dade County product approval for exterior-mounted equipment. Q10 - Is a bid bond required with the proposal, or are performance and payment bonds required only from the successful contractor after award? A10 - Please see responses above Q11 - For the 4-ton and 2-ton mini-split units identified for diagnosis, repair, or replacement, based on the current condition of the equipment, we believe replacement is the most appropriate option. Please confirm whether we may submit pricing based on complete replacement of these units. A11 - See A5. Offerors shall price complete replacement of both the Task 4 and Task 5 systems, including the outdoor condensing unit and the matching indoor unit. Permitting Q12 - Does this project require a Miami-Dade County mechanical permit for each unit, or does NOAA handle permitting internally for work on this campus? A12 - See A9. A Miami-Dade County mechanical permit is not required for this work. Q13 - If a county permit is needed, who submits the application, the contractor or NOAA? A13 - Not applicable. See A9. Q14 - Is the Miami-Dade product approval (NOA) documentation required before we submit our quote, or only later at the time of permit application? A14 - Product approval documentation is not required with the quote. Offerors should identify the proposed make and model in their technical approach. Documentation of Miami-Dade Notice of Acceptance or equivalent Florida product approval shall be provided to the technical point of contact prior to installation. Q15 - Is a stamped engineer drawing required for the rooftop package unit replacements, or are manufacturer spec sheets sufficient since it is a same-capacity swap? A15 - Manufacturer specification and cut sheets are sufficient. Signed and sealed engineering drawings are not required for like-for-like capacity replacement. Q16 - Who schedules and conducts inspections once the work is complete, a county inspector or someone from NOAA? A16 - Because no county permit is required for this work, there will be no county inspection. Government acceptance will be performed by the Contracting Officer or authorized representative per CAR 1352.246-70. The contractor shall contact the technical point of contact to walk the punch list and close out the project per Deliverable 5 of the SOW. Roof Condition Q17 - The roof stands for the rooftop units appear structurally sound, with the equipment itself showing the corrosion. If we are replacing the units, can the existing roof stands be kept as-is without resealing or replacement, or is that required regardless? A17 - The SOW requirement stands. Tasks 1 and 2 require the existing roof stand be repaired or replaced as required to properly support the new unit. The contractor shall assess each stand and repair or replace as needed. Existing stands may be reused only where structurally sound and free of significant section loss. New ductwork must be installed and sealed to the roof in all cases. Site Access Q18 - Do our technicians need a badge or facility ID to access the campus for each visit? A18 - A PIV or CAC is not required. Contractor personnel will be granted visitor access. The contractor shall provide a list of personnel names to the technical point of contact in advance of each visit. Personnel must present government-issued photo identification on arrival. Q19 - Is there a laydown area near the roof that could be reserved for our crane when installing the RTUs on the Annex? A19 - Yes. A staging and crane setup area near the Annex can be made available. The specific location and duration will be coordinated with the technical point of contact after award. The contractor is responsible for protecting pavement and for maintaining clear fire lanes and emergency vehicle access at all times. title: COMBINED SOURCES SOUGHT AND NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE FOR COMBINED ARMS VIRTUAL ENVIRONMENT TRAINER (CAVE) UPGRADE
description: ***THIS IS A COMBINED SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE AND NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE*** SPECIAL NOTICE: Combined Sources Sought and Notice of Intent to Sole Source This is a Combined Sources Sought Notice and Notice of Intent to Sole Source published in accordance with FAR 5.201 and FAR Part 10. The Department of War/ Naval Air Warfare Center Training Systems Division (NAWCTSD) intends to negotiate a sole-source contract with Battlespace Simulations LLC under the authority of FAR 6.302-1. This notice is published for market research purposes to determine if other responsible sources exist that can satisfy this requirement BACKGROUND The Naval Air Warfare Center Training Systems Division (NAWCTSD), Orlando, FL intends to sole source the effort to restore non-mission-capable Portable Lightweight Designator/Rangefinder (PLDR) and Common Laser Range Finder - Integrated Capability (CLRF-IC) targeting assets to a fully operational, calibrated, and deployable status to Battlespace Simulations LLC (BSI) (CAGE code 4KC80) of Lakewood Ranch, FL under the authority of 10 USC 2304 (c) (1) as implemented by FAR 6.302-1. BSI is the developer of the specialized software and custom firmware plug-in configurations integrated into these tactical units, and possesses the exclusive proprietary source code, technical data rights, and certified optical calibration chambers required to align the optics and certify that the lasers meet original MIL-SPEC eye-safe parameters. The Government does not have and cannot provide data rights to any software components that would be necessary to perform this upgrade. In order to comply with PGI 206.302-1, the Government is seeking information on the availability of potential comparable sources to upgrade the existing CAVE training systems capability located at Expeditionary Warfare Training Group, Pacific (EWTGPAC), Naval Amphibious Base (NAB) Coronado in San Diego, California (CA). BSI is the only responsible source capable of satisfying this requirement because they hold the proprietary technical data, software rights, and specialized calibration tooling necessary to return these military unique targeting systems to a mission-capable state. The updated hardware components utilized during the refurbishment process require a proprietary software firmware plug-in developed exclusively by BSI. Only BSI's engineering team possesses the proprietary source code and technical data rights to configure, install, and test this software on the PLDR and CLRF-IC systems. No other vendor can provide or support this critical interface software. HOW TO RESPOND TO THIS NOTICE In responding to this notice, please DO NOT PROVIDE PROPRIETARY INFORMATION. Submit the response by email to the Primary Point of Contact and, if specified, to the Secondary Point of Contact listed in this notice as soon as possible, and preferably before the closing date and time of this notice. Please review the attached PDF file for further details. IMPORTANT NOTES The information received in response to this notice will be reviewed and considered so that NAWCTSD may appropriately solicit for its requirements in the near future. This notice should not be construed as a commitment by NAWCTSD to issue a solicitation or ultimately award a contract. This notice is not a request for a quotation. Responses will not be considered as proposals or quotations. No award will be made as a result of this notice. NAWCTSD is not responsible for any costs incurred by the respondents to this notice. NAWCTSD reserves the right to use information provided by respondents for any purpose deemed necessary and appropriate. Thank you for taking the time to submit a response to this request!

title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source - ATC Radio Test System
description: Notice of Intent to Sole Source for Communication Service Monitor Test System 1. GENERAL INFORMATION: Notice ID: FA470426Q8001 Title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source - ATC Radio Test System NAICS Code: 334515 (Instrument Manufacturing for Measuring and Testing Electricity and Electrical Signals) PSC: 6625 (Electrical and Electronic Properties Measuring and Testing Instruments) Response Date: September 15, 2026, at 12:00 PM EDT 2. CONTRACTING OFFICE: Agency: Department of the Air Force, AFSOUTH Office: 346th Air Expeditionary Wing, 346th AEW/CONS Contracting Officer: James Bryan D. Buyag, SSgt, USAF Email: james_bryan.buyag@us.af.mil 3. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT: The Government requires the following items to support Radar, Airfield & Weather Systems (RAWS) maintenance and testing: CLIN 0001 (UOI: Each, QTY:1): A comprehensive Radio Frequency (RF) Communications Service Monitor equipped with an integrated Instrument Landing System (ILS) test suite. The complete test configuration must include: � Integrated Spectrum Analyzer (with tracking generator); � 1-Port Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) for VSWR and Distance-to-Fault (DTF) measurements; � Full-duplex transmitter/receiver testing capability; � Automated test, alignment, and simulcast modulation analysis modules; � Specialized interface cabling, adapter hardware, and pre-programmed automated test procedure setup files compatible with fielded General Dynamics CM-300/350 and URC-300 Air Traffic Control (ATC) radio. CLIN 0002 (UOI: Each, QTY:1): TACAN Power Sensor. A high-power sensor for Tactical Air Navigation (TACAN) system testing, with a frequency range of 960 MHz to 1215 MHz and a peak power measurement capability from 1700 W to 3600 W. CLIN 0003 (UOI: Each, QTY:1): External Power Sensor Support Module. A module to provide software support for an external power sensor compatible with the Bird RF 5017D sensor. CLIN 0004 (UOI: Each, QTY:1): Calibration Certificate. An ISO 9001 compliant calibration certificate for the test system. CLIN 0005 (UOI: Each, QTY:1): Hardware Warranty and Calibration Plan. A 5-year total hardware warranty and calibration service plan for the test system. 4. PROPOSED SOLE-SOURCE CONTRACTOR: Contractor Name: Testforce USA, Inc. CAGE: 7VPU9 UEI: PG22HN3Q3JM6 5. STATUTORY AUTHORITY & JUSTIFICATION: The proposed contract action is for a noncommercial supply for which the Government intends to solicit and negotiate with only one source under the authority of RFO 13.101 Simplified Procedures for Noncommercial Acquisitions. Testforce USA, Inc. (CAGE: 7VPU9) is the sole source capable of fulfilling this requirement: Proprietary Integration: In collaboration with the Air Force Flight Standards Agency (HQ AFFSA), Testforce developed proprietary automated test procedures, custom adapter/cabling kits, and specialized software setup files for the CX300 to test USAF CM300/350 and URC-300 radios, TACAN, and Instrument Landing Systems (ILS) in compliance with governing Technical Orders. OEM / Market Research Validation: While Viavi Solutions manufactures the baseline CX300 hardware, neither the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) nor any other third-party distributor possesses or licenses the proprietary preset files and custom interface kits developed by Testforce. Procuring standard OEM hardware without these proprietary assets would cause severe mission degradation, substantial duplication of cost, and unacceptable operational delays to independently develop and certify testing configurations. Integrated System Scope: All hardware modules, power sensors, calibration services, and warranty support listed are interdependent and required to maintain certified test accuracy for airfield navigation safety. No viable commercial or nondevelopmental alternatives exist. 6. INSTRUCTIONS TO INTERESTED PARTIES: This notice of intent is NOT a request for competitive quotes. However, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which the agency shall consider. Capability statements must demonstrate clear and convincing evidence that the submitter can provide an equivalent product that satisfies all Government technical and interface requirements, including the proprietary software and hardware integration. Submissions must be received electronically via email to the Contracting Officer @ james_bryan.buyag@us.af.mil no later than the response date and time listed in this notice. 7. DISCLAIMER: A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. The Government will not pay for any information submitted in response to this notice.

title: Laboratory Analysis - Phase II Environmental Site Assessment - Fort DuPont, Delaware City, DE
description: Introduction: It is the intent of the Government to award a sole source purchase order for analytical laboratory services from Alpha Analytical as cited in the attached Sole Source Justification. Under an Interagency Agreement, the U.S. Departme nt of Transportation John A. Volpe National Transportation Systems Center (Volpe Center) is providing support to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Targeted Brownfields Assessments (TBA) Program. As part of this effort, a Phase II Environmental Site Assessment (ESA) that includes a requirement for laboratory analysis will be conducted at the Fort DuPont Parade Ground (the Site) located at 260 Old Elm Ave, Delaware City, Delaware. Background: The objective of this Phase II ESA investigation is to determine if known contamination stemming from former military operations at the Fort DuPont property has impacted soil or groundwater at the Parade Ground (OU-9). Laboratory analytical data from soil and groundwater samples obtained through the advancement of soil borings and the installation of groundwater monitoring wells will be collected. Analytical results will be compared the Human Health and Ecological Screening Levels published in the Delaware Department of Natural Resources and Environmental Control (DNREC) Hazardous Substance Cleanup Act (HSCA) Screening Level Table Guidance Appendix A tables. Soil samples will be compared to the Soil (Direct Contract) HSCA Human Health Screening Levels and the Ecological Surface Soil Screening Levels. Groundwater samples will be compared to the Groundwater HSCA Human Health Screening Levels. Tasks to be Performed: The Phase II ESA investigation includes the Contractor tasks listed below. The Contractor shall conduct all work in accordance with Federal, State and local requirements. Where inconsistencies exist, the Contractor shall follow the most stringent requirements. 1) Sample Containers, Handling, and Delivery: The Contractor shall provide the appropriate sample containers, disposable volatiles samplers, preservatives, pre-printed labels, and analyte-free water required for the analyses listed below. These are to be delivered by the Contractor to the project site location. Sample collection and handling will be performed by Volpe personnel. The laboratory shall provide a daily local courier to transport the samples from the Site to the laboratory over an anticipated three days of sampling. Whenever possible, the Contractor shall minimize the number of sample containers by combining compatible analyses into a single container, as allowed by EPA methods and laboratory standard operating procedures. 2) Sample Analysis: Metals, Cyanide, VOCs, SVOCs, TPH-DRO, TPH GRO, PCBs, Pesticides, VOC Trip Blank, Metals, Cyanide, VOCs, SVOCs, TPH-DRO, TPH GRO, PCBs, Pesticides.

description: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation & Notice of Intent General Information Details Notice ID: FA9302-26-Q-0132 Notice Type: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation Contracting Office: AFTC/PZZG NAICS Code: 336413 - Other Aircraft Parts and Auxiliary Equipment Manufacturing PSC Code: 1680 - MISCELLANEOUS AIRCRAFT ACCESSORIES AND COMPONENTS Response Date: 15 September 2026, 10:00AM PST Description of Requirement This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with the format in Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Subpart 12.2, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. The Department of War (DoW) intends to negotiate on a sole source basis with MISSION SYSTEMS ORCHARD PARK INC (Legal Business Name: Eaton Corporation) for the procurement of Parachutist Oxygen Systems at Edwards AFB. Notice of Intent to Sole Source Subject Description Statutory Authority 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) as implemented by RFO 6.103-1 Justification In accordance with Air Force Instruction (AFI) 10-3503 (Personnel Parachute Program) and the authoritative policy memorandum issued by the Air Force Personnel Parachute Program (PPP) Office, Air Force personnel are strictly restricted to utilizing parachutist life-support equipment formally approved and published on the USAF PPP Approved For Use List (AUL). Only the Eaton PHANTOM Parachutist Oxygen Mask Assemblies, ground booster, and associated accessories are explicitly certified on the PPP AUL as authorized equipment for high-altitude military free-fall and static-line parachuting operations. Parachutist oxygen systems are critical life-support apparatuses operated in extreme, life-threatening high-altitude environments (up to 35,000+ ft MSL) where equipment malfunction or non-standard oxygen delivery rates result in rapid hypoxia, operational failure, severe injury, or death. Sourcing alternative commercial systems that lack formal PPP AUL certification violates Air Force safety policy and introduces unacceptable mission and life-safety risks. Scope of Work The contractor shall provide specified items in the Statement of Requirements Market Research The end users searched GSA for oxygen resulting in a singular retailer-Eaton. However, the required oxygen system parts do not appear on GSA. The contracting office then verified information provided by USAF SOCOM and found only Cobham items are approved, however Cobham was bought out by Eaton Corporation. FPDS-NG was searched for similar requirements utilizing the entity's UEI "JAGFLJSK5229" A few similar requirements for Phantom Oxygen systems were found. W911QY26FA132 in particular was similar in nature and value. The SME's were asked to provide the letter from USAF SOCOM and the source list was attached to the letter. Instructions to Interested Parties This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals; however, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation which shall be considered by the agency. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. Applicable Provisions & Clauses The following FAR/RFO provisions and clauses apply to this acquisition: Provision/Clause Title FAR 52.212-1 Instructions to Offerors - Commercial Products and Commercial Services FAR 52.212-3 Offeror Representations and Certifications - Commercial Products and Commercial Services FAR 52.212-4 Contract Terms and Conditions - Commercial Products and Commercial Services

description: NASA/AFRC has a requirement for facilities and utilities necessary to support PC-12 aircraft ground and flight operations during the QUARC laser communications campaign. title: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION -ADVANCE NOTICE TO INDUSTRY: Potential Use of Other Transaction Authority (OTA) for the Facilities Sustainment, Restoration, and Modernization (FSRM) Program at Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM)
description: 1. NOTICE AND DISCLAIMER This is a Request for Information (RFI) issued solely for market intelligence and acquisition planning purposes. It does not constitute a formal Solicitation, Request for Proposal (RFP), or Request for Qualifications (RFQ), and no solicitation is currently available. Participation in this RFI is strictly voluntary. The Government will not award any agreement or contract as a result of this notice, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs associated with preparing or submitting a response. Submission of a response does not obligate the Government in any way, and will not affect a firm's ability to submit a proposal should a formal solicitation be issued in the future. While Other Transaction (OT) Agreements executed under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a are not subject to standard FAR-based small business set-aside regulations, the Government is highly interested in understanding the size, demographics, and capabilities of the interested industrial base. 2. PURPOSE The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Seattle District, on behalf of Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM), is conducting market intelligence to explore the use of Other Transaction Authority (OTA) under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a to provide an innovative, programmatic approach to delivering its Facilities Sustainment, Restoration, and Modernization (FSRM) program. 3. PROGRAM OVERVIEW The scope of the JBLM FSRM Program includes operational facilities, training sites, administrative spaces, barracks/troop housing, utility infrastructure systems (HVAC, electrical, fire protection), and site work for JBLM Garrison facilities Projects will span multiple facility types across JBLM (Lewis Main, McChord Field, and Yakima Training Center). Projects will be primarily general construction activities including but not limited to: renovation, repairs, building expansions, and pre-engineered buildings (not to exceed the statutory limit for new construction), or repair by replacement. Scope may also include preventative maintenance, environmental abatement (e.g., asbestos and lead-based paint abatement), erosion control, and earthwork. Construction situations may include but are not limited to: civil, mechanical, plumbing, structural, electrical, heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC), fire protection systems, communications systems, and anti-terrorism and force protection. 4. POTENTIAL ACQUISITION STRATEGY The Government intends to establish a Master OT Agreement framework with the following characteristics: � Aggregate Program Value: Approximately $100 Million. � Structure: A single Master OT Agreement under which a pool of multiple pre-qualified design-build (or equivalent) teams will be established. � Period of Performance: A 5-year base period with the potential to extend to a total of 7 years. � Work Packages: Individual FSRM projects will be packaged and assigned to teams within the pre-qualified pool over the life of the agreement. � Project Delivery Methods: Individual work packages may be executed utilizing Progressive Design-Build (PDB), Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR), or other collaborative, fast-tracked commercial delivery methods tailored to the specific project. � Anticipated Two-Step Selection Process: To minimize bid-and-proposal costs for industry, the Government intends to utilize a streamlined, Qualifications-Based Selection (QBS) process to select the pool of partners: Step 1 (Request for Qualifications): Proposers submit a highly concise Statement of Qualifications (SOQ) focusing on team capability, alternative delivery past performance, and collaborative philosophy. No pricing will be evaluated. Step 2 (Pitch Presentations): Shortlisted firms will be invited to participate in confidential, interactive "Pitch Presentations" and workshops to evaluate team chemistry, real-time problem-solving, and open-book commercial capability. 5. ANTICIPATED INDUSTRY DAY USACE Seattle District anticipates hosting an Industry Day in the Seattle area on or about 20 October 2026. The Industry Day is intended to: � Provide an overview of the JBLM FSRM OTA concept, anticipated Master Agreement structure, and potential scope � Share the Government�s current thinking on delivery methods (including but not limited to Progressive Design-Build) � Obtain industry feedback on commercial practices, teaming, pricing approaches, risk allocation, and barriers to participation � Allow one-on-one or small-group discussions with interested firms (as capacity permits) Exact date, time, location, registration instructions, and agenda will be published in a subsequent notice (SAM.gov and/or direct distribution to respondents to this RFI). Firms that respond to this RFI will be prioritized for Industry Day communications. 6. RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS Interested parties are requested to submit responses by completing the online questionnaire at: https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/FeJXcQu89F The questionnaire is the Government's primary mechanism for obtaining detailed market intelligence and addresses industry capability, experience, technical capabilities, construction considerations, and recommended OTA and commercial practices. If necessary, interested parties may also submit a brief capabilities statement containing relevant information not otherwise addressed in the questionnaire. Capability statements shall not exceed 5 pages in length. The Government requests that firms avoid duplicating information already provided through the questionnaire. Supplemental capability statements are requested to be submitted via email to the individual(s) listed below no later than 10:00 AM Pacific Time on 15 September 2026. Late responses may still be considered at the Government�s discretion but are not guaranteed review prior to strategy finalization. Jeffrey Ross, Contracting Officer Brett Vegeto, Contracting Officer JBLM Special Projects Branch Contracting Division, Seattle District, Northwestern Division Email: jeffrey.a.ross@usace.army.mil Email: brett.s.vegeto@usace.army.mil Subject line: �RFI Response � JBLM FSRM Other Transaction Authority � [Firm Name]� The Government welcomes candid industry feedback and recommendations regarding commercial practices, agreement terms, project phasing, risk sharing, governance, pricing approaches, and other considerations that could improve successful execution of this project under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. Interested firms are encouraged to add themselves to the Interested Vendors List associated with this announcement on SAM.gov to receive future updates. Note: Do not submit proprietary trade secrets, protected technologies, or classified information in your response. All feedback received will be handled as public market research to shape the Government's final acquisition approach.

description: Concept Papers - Submissions will be accepted from July 15, 2024 � August 15, 2025. In response to this BAA solicitation, Concept Papers must be submitted to: VHASuicidePreventionBAA@va.gov As an innovation engine within the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), the vision of the VA Innovation Ecosystem (VHAIE) is a VA innovating at the forefront of science and research, service delivery, and employee empowerment. VHAIE leads this vision through development of organizational capability, delivery of operational breakthroughs, and by driving futures. VHAIE is committed to developing and employing agile mechanisms that allow VA to source incremental and transformational innovations to best serve Veterans and their families. This Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) opportunity seeks to source and fund early-stage research, development, prototyping, and piloting with an overall goal of moving forward the state of the art. VHAIE invites all potential offerors (including private sector companies, non-profits, and institutions of higher learning) to contribute ideas for innovations in SUICIDE prevention, care coordination, and treatment that significantly increase Veteran access to services, reduce or control costs of delivering those services, enhance the performance of VA operations, and improve the quality of service that Veterans and their families receive.

Defense Base Act (42 U.S.C. 1651 �DBA�) requires federal contractors and subcontractors working outside the continental United States to provide the equivalent of workers� compensation insurance to their employees. The U.S. Government reimburses DBA insurance carriers for claims paid in connection with injuries or deaths from war hazards as defined and covered by the War Hazards Compensation Act. According to the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR 28.305), contracting officers must include DBA (workers� compensation) insurance in each contract approved or financed under the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961, as amended (Public Law 87-195) unless the Secretary of Labor approves a waiver of coverage.

title: PTAG RFI: USPTO seeks Real Estate Planning & Management Support Services
description: ***9/4/26 AMENDED: in Acknowledgement of the holiday weekend, the deadline for questions has been extended to WEDNESDAY, SEPTEMBER 9, 2026 AT 1:00 PM ET*** THIS IS A PTAG SOURCES SOUGHT REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. This PTAG 6.1.1 Sources Sought (request for information) Notice (RFI) is strictly for market research ONLY. It is for informational and planning purposes and shall NOT be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation or commitment by the Government at this time. PTAG The Government contemplates utilizing the Alternative Competition Method in accordance with the Patent and Trademark Office Acquisition Guidelines (PTAG) and the Patent and Trademark Office Efficiency Act 35 U.S.C. 2(b)(4)(A). This Sources sought notice is intended as preliminary market information gathering which the United States patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) will use to determine which small business contractor(s) is/are the most likely to successfully meet the agency�s needs and are thereby eligible to participate in an alternative competition. As a result of this market research, the solicitation will only be issued to the/ those qualified small business contractor(s) that is/are deemed most likely to successfully meet the agency�s requirements as stated below. This RFI is being made available under NAICS: 531210 - Offices of Real Estate Agents and Brokers and PSC R499 - SUPPORT- PROFESSIONAL: OTHER Purpose of this Sources Sought / Request for Information (RFI) The USPTO Office of the Chief Administrative Officer (OCAO), seeks a contractor to provide real estate portfolio management support services to include real property planning support and to assist the USPTO on all negotiations and discussions related to its GSA leasehold interests for the Alexandria Campus and Detroit Regional Office. In addition, support may be requested to assist the USPTO to make long-term planning decisions for each of the facilities within the USPTO�s portfolio. Currently, these facilities include the Dallas Regional Office located in a GSA owned facility; and the San Jose Regional Office which is directly leased by the USPTO. Real property planning support is required for all USPTO�s real property holdings. USPTO, as a tenant, must develop and implement a real estate portfolio strategy to secure, right-size, and maintain agency space needs without disruption. This contract will enable USPTO to mitigate resource constraints and improve efficiency, while securing technical data and expertise to ensure the implementation of an effective real property strategy going forward. Current Office Locations Main campus headquarters: 600 Dulany Street, Alexandria Virginia which is GSA leased space for which USPTO has separate occupancy agreements for each of the following buildings: Madison East/ Madison West , Knox, and Jefferson. USPTO directly leases one garage structure (East Garage) housing 1780 parking spaces directly connected to the main campus A GSA leased warehouse in Lorton VA. GSA owned warehouse in Springfield VA. Current Regional Offices: Detroit RO: 300 River Place, Detroit, Michigan. GSA leased space Dallas RO: 207 S. Houston St, Dallas, Texas. GSA owned facility San Jose RO: 200 E. Santa Clara St, San Jose, California. The response to this RFI should provide OCAO management with an understanding of the contractor�s experience and the range of services provided. This will allow USPTO to conduct thorough market research, identify suitable providers, and make informed decisions. HOW TO RESPOND TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE All interested contractors should provide the following information in their response via e-mail to the contacts listed below: The name of your contractor, address, SAM UEI, point of contact information, email, phone, website address. Your FSS Schedule contract number (Only if applicable). Proof your contractor is a small business under NAICS 531210 Any relevant certifications or other relevant authorizations Information about your contractor�s ability to meet the requirements stated above by providing enough detail to show: Past performance should include twenty plus years of real estate analysis and planning experience with the GSA policies and procedures and engagement in the areas of space strategies, POR requirements, and lease negotiations. Understanding of current USPTO space standards, business units, regional functionality and operations, and unique staff requirements as it pertains to the various unions. Demonstrated experience with federal government real estate policy, procurement process, federal government program of requirements development, leveraging experience with the GSA, evaluation practices and lease negotiations. Demonstrated expertise in working with the GSA, OMB and Congress for federal office space leasing acquisition. Expert level experience in strategic planning and programming, conceptual and schematic design, design development, construction and contract documents, and project administration. Key Personnel In your response to this source sought, please identify any Key Personnel that would likely be involved in fulfilling the requirements, and include any relevant background information on those individuals. QUESTIONS Questions regarding this RFI are due no later than September 9. 2026 at 1:00 PM ET and are to be submitted via eBUY and/or email to Kendall.jones1@uspto.gov and christopher.ward@uspto.gov NO PHONE CALLS PLEASE DEADLINE: Responses are due no later than September 15. 2026 at 1:00 PM ET and are to be submitted via eBUY and/or email to Kendall.jones1@uspto.gov and christopher.ward@uspto.gov Late responses may be considered at the government�s discretion. Disclaimer: This PTAG Sources Sought Request For Information (RFI) notice is issued solely for Market Research information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation. All information received in response to this RFI that is marked as proprietary will be handled in accordance with procurement integrity requirements. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI.

description: USDA�s response to the New World Screwworm (NWS) is a top priority. Its National Detector Dog Training Center (NDDTC) in Newnan, GA, is expanding its NWS training program to strengthen USDA�s operational readiness and ensure canine teams are fully prepared for field conditions. Recent pilot activities in Texas demonstrated that NWS detector dogs must be safely acclimated to livestock environments including interactions with cattle, sheep, and goats to build the skills necessary for effective detection in real?world settings. To support this requirement, NDDTC must maintain goats onsite as essential training aids. Establishing appropriate housing, fencing, shelter, and utilities is a foundational step to ensure the animals� welfare, comply with applicable standards, and provide consistent access to training environments that accurately simulate operational livestock settings. The contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, and expertise necessary to design, construct, and install fenced livestock enclosures, shelters, flooring, utilities, water systems, and a simulated chute?training environment to support on?site goat housing and NWS canine training. All work must comply with USDA facility, animal?welfare, and safety standards and integrate with existing NDDTC infrastructure. NOTE: Quotes are required by Sept 8. Time is of the essence for this requirement as the government requires rapid delivery. The Contractor will be required to (a) commence work under this contract immediately upon receipt of the NTP, (b) prosecute the work diligently, and (c) complete the entire work ready for use by October 30, 2026.. title: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION -ADVANCE NOTICE TO INDUSTRY: Potential Use of Other Transaction Authority (OTA) for the Facilities Sustainment, Restoration, and Modernization (FSRM) Program at Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM)
description: 1. NOTICE AND DISCLAIMER This is a Request for Information (RFI) issued solely for market intelligence and acquisition planning purposes. It does not constitute a formal Solicitation, Request for Proposal (RFP), or Request for Qualifications (RFQ), and no solicitation is currently available. Participation in this RFI is strictly voluntary. The Government will not award any agreement or contract as a result of this notice, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs associated with preparing or submitting a response. Submission of a response does not obligate the Government in any way, and will not affect a firm's ability to submit a proposal should a formal solicitation be issued in the future. While Other Transaction (OT) Agreements executed under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a are not subject to standard FAR-based small business set-aside regulations, the Government is highly interested in understanding the size, demographics, and capabilities of the interested industrial base. 2. PURPOSE The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Seattle District, on behalf of Joint Base Lewis-McChord (JBLM), is conducting market intelligence to explore the use of Other Transaction Authority (OTA) under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a to provide an innovative, programmatic approach to delivering its Facilities Sustainment, Restoration, and Modernization (FSRM) program. 3. PROGRAM OVERVIEW The scope of the JBLM FSRM Program includes operational facilities, training sites, administrative spaces, barracks/troop housing, utility infrastructure systems (HVAC, electrical, fire protection), and site work for JBLM Garrison facilities Projects will span multiple facility types across JBLM (Lewis Main, McChord Field, and Yakima Training Center). Projects will be primarily general construction activities including but not limited to: renovation, repairs, building expansions, and pre-engineered buildings (not to exceed the statutory limit for new construction), or repair by replacement. Scope may also include preventative maintenance, environmental abatement (e.g., asbestos and lead-based paint abatement), erosion control, and earthwork. Construction situations may include but are not limited to: civil, mechanical, plumbing, structural, electrical, heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC), fire protection systems, communications systems, and anti-terrorism and force protection. 4. POTENTIAL ACQUISITION STRATEGY The Government intends to establish a Master OT Agreement framework with the following characteristics: � Aggregate Program Value: Approximately $100 Million. � Structure: A single Master OT Agreement under which a pool of multiple pre-qualified design-build (or equivalent) teams will be established. � Period of Performance: A 5-year base period with the potential to extend to a total of 7 years. � Work Packages: Individual FSRM projects will be packaged and assigned to teams within the pre-qualified pool over the life of the agreement. � Project Delivery Methods: Individual work packages may be executed utilizing Progressive Design-Build (PDB), Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR), or other collaborative, fast-tracked commercial delivery methods tailored to the specific project. � Anticipated Two-Step Selection Process: To minimize bid-and-proposal costs for industry, the Government intends to utilize a streamlined, Qualifications-Based Selection (QBS) process to select the pool of partners: Step 1 (Request for Qualifications): Proposers submit a highly concise Statement of Qualifications (SOQ) focusing on team capability, alternative delivery past performance, and collaborative philosophy. No pricing will be evaluated. Step 2 (Pitch Presentations): Shortlisted firms will be invited to participate in confidential, interactive "Pitch Presentations" and workshops to evaluate team chemistry, real-time problem-solving, and open-book commercial capability. 5. ANTICIPATED INDUSTRY DAY USACE Seattle District anticipates hosting an Industry Day in the Seattle area on or about 20 October 2026. The Industry Day is intended to: � Provide an overview of the JBLM FSRM OTA concept, anticipated Master Agreement structure, and potential scope � Share the Government�s current thinking on delivery methods (including but not limited to Progressive Design-Build) � Obtain industry feedback on commercial practices, teaming, pricing approaches, risk allocation, and barriers to participation � Allow one-on-one or small-group discussions with interested firms (as capacity permits) Exact date, time, location, registration instructions, and agenda will be published in a subsequent notice (SAM.gov and/or direct distribution to respondents to this RFI). Firms that respond to this RFI will be prioritized for Industry Day communications. 6. RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS Interested parties are requested to submit responses by completing the online questionnaire at: https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/FeJXcQu89F The questionnaire is the Government's primary mechanism for obtaining detailed market intelligence and addresses industry capability, experience, technical capabilities, construction considerations, and recommended OTA and commercial practices. If necessary, interested parties may also submit a brief capabilities statement containing relevant information not otherwise addressed in the questionnaire. Capability statements shall not exceed 5 pages in length. The Government requests that firms avoid duplicating information already provided through the questionnaire. Supplemental capability statements are requested to be submitted via email to the individual(s) listed below no later than 10:00 AM Pacific Time on 15 September 2026. Late responses may still be considered at the Government�s discretion but are not guaranteed review prior to strategy finalization. Jeffrey Ross, Contracting Officer Brett Vegeto, Contracting Officer JBLM Special Projects Branch Contracting Division, Seattle District, Northwestern Division Email: jeffrey.a.ross@usace.army.mil Email: brett.s.vegeto@usace.army.mil Subject line: �RFI Response � JBLM FSRM Other Transaction Authority � [Firm Name]� The Government welcomes candid industry feedback and recommendations regarding commercial practices, agreement terms, project phasing, risk sharing, governance, pricing approaches, and other considerations that could improve successful execution of this project under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. Interested firms are encouraged to add themselves to the Interested Vendors List associated with this announcement on SAM.gov to receive future updates. Note: Do not submit proprietary trade secrets, protected technologies, or classified information in your response. All feedback received will be handled as public market research to shape the Government's final acquisition approach.

description: Předmětem veřejné zakázky je zpracování projektové dokumentace, dodávka a následná realizace díla s názvem „9856- Náhrada havarijních čerpadel bóru 2. HVB, systém TB1 (typ 3CHG-6K-14-2, CG-50/50K-15-1)“ v JE Dukovany formou vyšší kompletované dodávky souboru strojů a zařízení a provedení všech nutně vyvolaných a požadovaných úprav na dotčených zařízeních, konstrukcích a systémech. V rámci realizace JMA 9856 Dodavatel provede na zvolených pozicích náhradu havarijních podávacích čerpadel roztoku kyseliny borité 3,4TB20,40,60D01 typu 3CHG-6K-14-2 a typu CG-50/50K-15-1. Jedná se celkem o 6 ks čerpadel. Jsou požadována čerpadla v bez ucpávkovém provedení (s magnetickou spojkou) a samostatným motorem, chlazená okolním vzduchem. Součástí výměny je úprava navazujících potrubních tras sání a výtlaku, navazující potrubí recirkulace a drenáže a úprava uchycení nového čerpadla dle nově vybraného soustrojí. Zhotovitel provede úpravu podpůrných ocelových konstrukcí v rozsahu nezbytném pro instalaci nových čerpadel a úpravu stávajícího betonového základu. Dále proběhne výměna kabeláže z přechodových skříněk po pohon a zrušení samostatného uzavřeného chladícího okruhu čerpadel. Přesné vymezení Předmětu veřejné zakázky a ostatní požadavky na jeho provedení včetně informací, podmínek, specifikací a ostatních údajů jsou detailně specifikovány v části 3 a 4 Zadávací dokumentace.

Description of Requirement: AIRCRAFT LIFTING SYSTEMS FOR CRASH DAMAGE OR DISABLED AIRCRAFT RECOVERY (CDDAR) The Volk Field Air National Guard Base requires the procurement of specialized Crash Damage or Disabled Aircraft Recovery (CDDAR) equipment to maintain mission readiness and ensure safe recovery operations. The required items include: 15?Ton Pneumatic Aircraft Lifting Air Bag Stations (Part Number: 9314-010, Model 9314-010), a Control Console (Part Number: 9316-010, Control Console for Model 9314 010), and a Fuselage Lifting System capable of supporting both narrow?body and wide?body aircraft. title: Request for Information: Small Business Participation Goals- John Day Overhead Lifting Devices Repair
description: 1. NOTICE AND DISCLAIMER This is a Request for Information (RFI) issued solely for market intelligence and acquisition planning purposes. It does not constitute a formal Solicitation, Request for Proposal (RFP), or Request for Qualifications (RFQ), and no solicitation is currently available. Participation in this RFI is strictly voluntary. The Government will not award any agreement or contract as a result of this notice, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs associated with preparing or submitting a response. Submission of a response does not obligate the Government in any way and will not affect a firm's ability to submit a proposal should formal solicitation be issued in the future. NAICS Code: 238290 � Other Building Equipment Contractors. Small Business Size Standard at $22 million. 2. PURPOSE U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Portland District is requesting industry input on Small Business Subcontract Goals for an upcoming solicitation. 3. SCOPE OF WORK Contractor will pick-up five below-the-hook (BTH) lifting devices from the John Day powerhouse, remove and dispose of lead paint from the devices, make critical weld repairs at an off-site shop, paint the lifting devices, perform 125% load testing, and return the devices to John Day powerhouse. Devices are considered real property. Magnitude of Construction is $1,000,000 and $5,000,000. 4. GOALS Category Suggested Small Business Subcontracting Goals SB 50.0% SDB 3.0% WOSB 7.0% HUBZone Best Effort - 0.5% VOSB 22.0% SDVOSB 6.0% 5. REQUESTED FEEDBACK / RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS The Government requests industry feedback on the suggested Small Business subcontracting goals identified in this RFI. Respondents are encouraged to review the scope of work and provide input on whether the proposed goals are realistic, challenging and attainable for this requirement. If a respondent believes alternative goals would be more appropriate, the respondent is encouraged to propose recommended counter-goals and provide the supporting rationale. At a minimum, respondents are requested to address the following: a. description: This is a Sources Sought notice for market research purposes only. This is not a request for quotation (RFQ) or a solicitation. The 176th Wing (176WG), Alaska Air National Guard (AKANG), intends to award a single-award, sole-source Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) with a five (5) year ordering period to Nahtsiith LLC (dba Anchorage Wolverines). This action is prepared in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 13.106-1(b), which allows for soliciting from a single source when the contracting officer determines that only one source is reasonably available. The Government�s minimum need is for a strategic sponsorship with a premier, high-level junior sports franchise in Anchorage that attracts a dedicated, high-volume audience of families, young athletes, and community members throughout a regular sports season. The requirements in the PWS are intrinsically linked to the unique assets, exclusive branding rights, audience, and environment proprietary to the Anchorage Wolverines franchise during their events at the Sullivan Arena. NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is committed to fair, transparent, and efficient acquisitions. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek resolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the UDSA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.
