title: 176WG - Sources Sought/Intent to Award Sole Source for Strategic Community Sponsorship Program: People Mover Bus Wraps
description: This is a Sources Sought notice for market research purposes only. This is not a request for quotation (RFQ) or a solicitation. The Government will not pay for any information received in response to this notice. The 176th Wing (176WG), Alaska Air National Guard (AKANG), intends to award a sole-source, firm-fixed-price contract to Alaska Channel Inc. in Anchorage, AK. This action is prepared in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 13.106-1(b), which allows for soliciting from a single source when the contracting officer determines that only one source is reasonably available. The Government requires a commercial mobile advertising package to support the 176th Wing's recruiting and community engagement mission. Specifically, the requirement is for the final formatting, production, installation, and annual placement of one (1) full bus wrap on the Anchorage People Mover municipal transit system. A Draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) is attached to this notice for review. The determination to pursue a sole-source award is based on the assessment that Alaska Channel Inc. holds the exclusive municipal contract and legal authority to sell, manage, and place exterior advertising (including full bus wraps) on the Municipality of Anchorage�s People Mover transit fleet. Therefore, they are the only source reasonably available to satisfy the Government's requirement for this specific mobile advertising avenue. Instructions for Interested Parties: All responsible sources that believe they can meet the full requirements outlined in the attached Draft PWS are invited to submit a detailed capability statement. Capability statements must be submitted electronically to the Point of Contact listed above no later than the response date and time. To be considered a viable alternative source, the capability statement must provide clear and convincing evidence of the offeror's legal authority and technical capability to provide the exact same services, specifically including: Proof of the explicit, legal authority and approved municipal access to produce, install, and place full bus wrap advertising on active buses within the Municipality of Anchorage's People Mover transit fleet. A detailed description of the offeror's ability to meet every production and installation requirement listed in the attached Draft PWS, including strict adherence to Municipality formatting and safety specifications. General marketing capabilities, offerings for private transportation fleets, or offerings for transit systems outside of the Municipality of Anchorage will not be considered responsive to the Government's minimum need. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed requirement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Attachments: Draft PWS - People Mover Advertising

title: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE FOR PROJECT LABOR AGGREEMENTS (PLAs) TO COASTAL STORM RISK MANAGEMENT (CSRM) FOR CAPE MAY TO LOWER TOWNSHIP, NEW JERSEY, BRIGANTINE INLET TO GREAT EGG HARBOR INLET (ABSECON ISLAND), NEW JERSEY, AND BARNEGAT INLET TO LITTLE EGG, INLET
description: The US Army Corps of Engineers, Enterprise Dredge Delivery Center (EDDC), is soliciting comments from the construction community addressing the potential use of Project Labor Agreements (PLA) for a large-scale construction project (exceeding $35 million) within the Cape May To Lower Township, New Jersey, Brigantine Inlet To Great Egg Harbor Inlet (Absecon Island), New Jersey, And Barnegat Inlet To Little Egg, Inlet (Long Beach Island), New Jersey area. This procurement is for Coastal Storm Risk Management (CSRM). Cape May to Lower Township, NJ (Navigation Mitigation � Beachfill): Work for the beachfill placement dredging will require a hopper and pipeline/mechanical dredge(s). The dredge(s) must have the capability to dredge material up to a depth of -40 ft NAVD88 and to transport the dredged sand to the designated areas approximately 2.6 miles away. The project for navigation mitigation (beach nourishment) is located on the Atlantic coast of New Jersey, extending from the Cape May Inlet southwest jetty to the 3rd Ave terminal groin in Cape May City. It includes the communities of the City of Cape May and Lower Township, and the US Coast Guard Training Center. The contract work will consist of a base bid to conduct pre-placement condition surveys and pump/place 600,000 cubic yards of sand from two borrow areas approximately 2.6 miles south of the Cape May Inlet jetties onto the beach at 2 locations: Area 1 (540,000 cu yds), the US Coast Guard Training Center and Area 2 (60,000 cu yds), Wilmington Ave. Options to place additional sand (100,000 cu yds) from the same borrow areas to achieve the full project design template at these same two beach locations will also be included. Sand must come from the offshore borrow areas. Trucking-in sand will not be permitted under this contract. All work under the contract must be completed no later than 1 March 2028. Brigantine Inlet to Great Egg Harbor Inlet (Absecon Island), NJ (CSRM � Beachfill): Contract work consists of a base bid to place approximately 1,500,000 cubic yards of beachfill, along the Atlantic Ocean coastline of Absecon Island, Atlantic County, New Jersey. The project area encompasses the municipalities of Atlantic City, Ventnor, Margate, and Longport. The contract work may also consist of separate options to place additional amounts of beachfill per option, if awarded, in locations within and outside of the Base bid areas. The project work for the Base Bid and Options, if awarded, also may include, in addition to beachfill: the construction or repair of pedestrian, vehicle, and ADA compliant dune crossovers; planting dune grass; installing sand fencing; the repair or extension of existing storm water outfalls and drainage structures; and the relocation or removal of various existing structures or fill to accommodate the beachfill and dunes. The beachfill material for this contract must come from the authorized borrow areas, which are shown on the contract drawings, located within and adjacent to the Absecon Inlet in the Atlantic Ocean, and a separate designated area located approximately 2 � 3 miles offshore of Absecon Island in the Atlantic Ocean. Barnegat Inlet to Little Egg, Inlet (Long Beach Island), NJ (CSRM � Beachfill): Contract work consists of a base bid to place approximately 2,000,000 cubic yards of beachfill to repair the dune and berm system along the Atlantic Ocean coastline of Long Beach Island, Ocean County, New Jersey. The project area encompasses the municipalities of Long Beach Township, Borough of Harvey Cedars, Borough of Surf City, Borough of Ship Bottom, and Borough of Beach Haven. The contract work may also consist of separate options to place additional amounts of beachfill per option, if awarded, in locations within and outside of the Base bid areas. The project work for the Base Bid and Options, if awarded, also may include, in addition to beachfill: the construction or repair of pedestrian, vehicle, and ADA compatible dune crossovers; planting dune grass; providing sand fencing; and the relocation or removal of various existing structures to accommodate the beachfill, dunes and other project features. The beachfill material for this contract must come from the authorized borrow areas located approximately 2-3 miles offshore of Long Beach Island in the Atlantic Ocean, and/or the Little Egg Inlet as designated on the contract drawings. The solicitation is expected to be available in FY2027. A PLA is defined as a pre-hire collective bargaining agreement with one or more labor organizations that establishes the terms and conditions of employment for a specific construction project and is an agreement described in 29 U.S.C 158(f). Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Policy: (a) Project Labor Agreement (PLA) is a tool that agencies may use to promote economy and efficiency in Federal procurement. Pursuant to Executive Order 14063, agencies are encouraged to consider requiring the use of project labor agreements in connection with large-scale construction projects. (b) An agency may, if appropriate, require that every contractor and subcontractor engaged in construction on the project agree, for that project, to negotiate or become a party to a project labor agreement with one or more labor organizations if the agency decides that the use of project labor agreements will (1) Advance the Federal Government's interest in achieving economy and efficiency in Federal procurement, producing labor-management stability, and ensuring compliance with laws and regulations governing safety and health, equal employment opportunity, labor and employment standards, and other matters; and (2) Be consistent with law. Reference: Provision: 52.222-33 Notice of Requirement for Project Labor Agreement and Clause 52.222-34 Project Labor Agreement. (i) Requested are responses to the following: 1) Do you have knowledge that a PLA has been used in the local area on projects of this kind? If so, please provide supporting documentation. 2) Are you aware of skilled labor shortages in the area for those crafts that will be needed to complete the referenced project? If so, please elaborate and provide supporting documentation where possible. 3) Are you aware of time sensitive issues/scheduling requirements that would affect the rate at which the referenced project should be completed? If so, please elaborate and provide supporting documentation where possible. 4) Identify specific reasons why or how you believe a PLA would advance the Federal Government�s interest in achieving economy and efficiency in Federal procurement. 5) Identify specific reasons why you do not believe a PLA would advance the Federal Government�s interest in achieving economy and efficiency in Federal procurement. 6) Identify any additional information you believe the Government should take into consideration regarding the use of a PLA on the referenced project. 7) Does your company intend to bid/propose on this project if a PLA requirement is included in the solicitation? Does your company intend to bid/propose on this project if a PLA requirement is not included in the solicitation? 8) What are the likely cost impacts, if any, to your bid/proposal price if a PLA requirement is included in the solicitation? Please provide as much detail as possible regarding any anticipated cost impacts (positive or negative) of the inclusion of a PLA requirement, including any information you can provide about the magnitude of the anticipated impact. (ii) The information gathered in this exercise should include the following information on projects completed in the last 2-5 years (or other timeframe, as appropriate): 1) Project Name and Location: 2) Detailed Project Description: 3) Initial Cost Estimate vs. Actual Final Cost: 4) Was the project completed on time? 5) Number of craft trades present on the project: 6) Was a PLA used? 7) Were there any challenges experienced during the project? Responses shall be submitted via email to Terri Adams

title: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE FOR PROJECT LABOR AGGREEMENTS (PLAs) TO COASTAL STORM RISK MANAGEMENT (CSRM) FOR BETHANY BEACH AND SOUTH BETHANY BEACH, DE (CSRM - BEACHFILL), FENWICK ISLAND, DE (CSRM � BEACHFILL), REHOBOTH BEACH & DEWEY BEACH, DE (CSRM � BEACHFILL)
description: The US Army Corps of Engineers, Enterprise Dredge Delivery Center (EDDC), is soliciting comments from the construction community addressing the potential use of Project Labor Agreements (PLA) for a large-scale construction project (exceeding $35 million) within the Bethany Beach and South Bethany Beach, DE (CSRM - Beachfill), Fenwick Island, DE (CSRM � Beachfill), and Rehoboth Beach & Dewey Beach, DE (CSRM � Beachfill): areas. This procurement is for Coastal Storm Risk Management (CSRM). Bethany Beach and South Bethany Beach, DE (CSRM - Beachfill): The work for the Bethany Beach and South Bethany Beach, CRSM projects will include periodic renourishment of the beach berm and dune to the original design template. It is estimated that approximately 532,000 cubic yards of sand would be required to restore Bethany Beach and South Bethany Beach to the original design template and approximately 165,000 CY of optional sand could be provided for advanced nourishment for the project. The base bid work would also include repair/replacement of dune grass, fencing and crossovers. Borrow Area E will be the source used for sand to restore this beach area and will require the use of a hopper or hydraulic cutterhead since Borrow Area E is located approximately two to three miles offshore of the Town of South Bethany. Fenwick Island, DE (CSRM � Beachfill): The work for the Fenwick Island, CRSM project will include periodic renourishment of the beach berm and dune to the original design template. It is estimated that approximately 207,000 cubic yards of sand would be required to restore Fenwick Island to the original design template and approximately 60,000 CY of optional sand could be provided for advanced nourishment for the project. The base bid work would also include repair/replacement of dune grass, fencing and crossovers. The Fenwick Island borrow area will be the source used for sand to restore this beach area and will require the use of a hopper or hydraulic cutterhead since the Fenwick Borrow Area is located approximately one to three miles offshore of the Town of Fenwick Island. Rehoboth Beach & Dewey Beach, DE (CSRM � Beachfill): The work for the Rehoboth Beach to Dewey Beach, CRSM projects will include periodic renourishment of the beach berm and dune to the original design template. It is estimated that approximately 390,000 cubic yards of sand would be required to restore Rehoboth Beach and Dewey Beach to the design template and approximately 120,000 CY of optional sand could be provided for advanced nourishment for the project. The base bid work would also include repair/replacement of dune grass, fencing and crossovers. Borrow Area B will be the source used for sand to restore this beach area and will require the use of a hopper dredge due to the four to six mile transit distance that must be made in the Atlantic Ocean to travel to and from the sand borrow area. The solicitation is expected to be available in FY2027. A PLA is defined as a pre-hire collective bargaining agreement with one or more labor organizations that establishes the terms and conditions of employment for a specific construction project and is an agreement described in 29 U.S.C 158(f). Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Policy: (a) Project Labor Agreement (PLA) is a tool that agencies may use to promote economy and efficiency in Federal procurement. Pursuant to Executive Order 14063, agencies are encouraged to consider requiring the use of project labor agreements in connection with large-scale construction projects. (b) An agency may, if appropriate, require that every contractor and subcontractor engaged in construction on the project agree, for that project, to negotiate or become a party to a project labor agreement with one or more labor organizations if the agency decides that the use of project labor agreements will (1) Advance the Federal Government's interest in achieving economy and efficiency in Federal procurement, producing labor-management stability, and ensuring compliance with laws and regulations governing safety and health, equal employment opportunity, labor and employment standards, and other matters; and (2) Be consistent with law. Reference: Provision: 52.222-33 Notice of Requirement for Project Labor Agreement and Clause 52.222-34 Project Labor Agreement. (i) Requested are responses to the following: 1) Do you have knowledge that a PLA has been used in the local area on projects of this kind? If so, please provide supporting documentation. 2) Are you aware of skilled labor shortages in the area for those crafts that will be needed to complete the referenced project? If so, please elaborate and provide supporting documentation where possible. 3) Are you aware of time sensitive issues/scheduling requirements that would affect the rate at which the referenced project should be completed? If so, please elaborate and provide supporting documentation where possible. 4) Identify specific reasons why or how you believe a PLA would advance the Federal Government�s interest in achieving economy and efficiency in Federal procurement. 5) Identify specific reasons why you do not believe a PLA would advance the Federal Government�s interest in achieving economy and efficiency in Federal procurement. 6) Identify any additional information you believe the Government should take into consideration regarding the use of a PLA on the referenced project. 7) Does your company intend to bid/propose on this project if a PLA requirement is included in the solicitation? Does your company intend to bid/propose on this project if a PLA requirement is not included in the solicitation? 8) What are the likely cost impacts, if any, to your bid/proposal price if a PLA requirement is included in the solicitation? Please provide as much detail as possible regarding any anticipated cost impacts (positive or negative) of the inclusion of a PLA requirement, including any information you can provide about the magnitude of the anticipated impact. (ii) The information gathered in this exercise should include the following information on projects completed in the last 2-5 years (or other timeframe, as appropriate): 1) Project Name and Location 2) Detailed Project Description 3) Initial Cost Estimate vs. Actual Final Cost 4) Was the project completed on time? 5) Number of craft trades present on the project 6) Was a PLA used? 7) Were there any challenges experienced during the project? Responses shall be submitted via email to Melissa Vaughn at melissa.a.vaughn@usace.army.mil and Ros Shoemaker at rosalind.m.shoemaker@usace.army.mil no later than 3:00 PM EDT on 15 September 2026. The email should be titled: Delaware CSRM PLA Response This is NOT a Request for Proposal and does not constitute any commitment by the Government. Responses to this labor market survey will be used by the Government to make appropriate acquisition decisions. All interested sources must respond to future solicitation announcements separately from responses to this survey.

title: H142--Intent to Sole Source VASNHS Pharmacy Hood Testing and Certification
description: The Department of Veterans Affairs, Southern Nevada VA Healthcare System, intends to award a firm-fixed-price, sole source contract to Technical Safety Services (TSS) for specialized cleanroom certification, environmental monitoring, and testing services required for multiple pharmacy and compounding areas within the medical center. TSS is the only known vendor capable of providing all required semi annual, annual, and monthly testing services in accordance with USP <797>, USP <800>, CETA standards, and VA healthcare performance requirements. These services include airflow and leak testing, particle counting, airflow visualization studies, viable air and surface sampling, room pressure and air exchange verification, laminar flow unit and isolator certification, and preparation of formal compliance documentation. The integrated nature of these services requires a vendor with established expertise, calibrated instrumentation, and the ability to perform testing without disrupting critical pharmacy operations. Based on the Government s market research and previous performance history, no other vendor has demonstrated the ability to meet all required service frequencies, technical specifications, compliance standards, and facility specific operational needs. Estimated Contract Value: Total Estimated Value: $164,396.48 CATEGORY: RESPONSE FROM INTERESTED BUSINESSES Businesses that believe they are capable of providing the required services may submit a capability statement demonstrating their ability to meet all technical, regulatory, and performance requirements described in this notice. Interested businesses must provide the following information: Company Name, UEI Number, and Business Size Classification (e.g., SDVOSB, VOSB, small business, etc.). Evidence of Technical Capability, including: Demonstrated experience performing USP <797> and <800> compliant testing. Documentation showing CETA-compliant certification capabilities. Proof of calibrated instruments and ability to conduct all service categories listed in the Base and Option Year schedules. Past Performance, specifically for VA medical centers, DoD facilities, or other hospital cleanroom environments. Ability to Meet Required Frequencies and Scope, including semi annual, annual, and monthly testing. Statement of Availability, confirming your ability to perform services onsite in Southern Nevada. Any Additional Supporting Evidence demonstrating why your business can fully meet the Government s needs. Deadline for Submission: All capability statements must be submitted no later than September 15, 2026, at 12:00 PM PST. Submission Method: Email responses to the Contracting Office at[insert contracting officer s email] with the subject line: Response to Intent to Sole Source Southern Nevada VA Cleanroom Certification Services Late submissions may not be considered.

title: Public Environmental Services at Downtown BID
description: Notice of Intent to Issue a Sole Source Contract for public environmental services around the commercial and office buildings, as well as the public spaces within the Downtown BID jurisdiction in Washington DC. Description: The General Services Administration (GSA) Public Building Service (PBS) Acquisition Center for Facilities Management Services (ACFMS) - East intends to issue a sole source contract in accordance with FAR 6.103-1. The proposed contract will include a twelve-month base period and three twelve-month option periods. The contract work will be performed at the Downtown BID jurisdiction in Washington DC. The contract will provide the following services: Cleanliness, Maintenance and Beautification Supplement municipal trash collection by bagging, hauling, and compacting trash and recycling from cans and the ground around GSA buildings for collection by the Department of Public Works. Remove graffiti and other applied vandalism from buildings, sidewalks, and fixtures within 24 hours. Clean dirt, litter, and grime from sidewalks around GSA buildings, and power clean sidewalks and public spaces on a regular basis. Remove gum and gum stains from sidewalks around GSA buildings using specialized mechanical equipment. Paint and visually improve public space elements around GSA buildings, including benches, trash receptacles, poles, lights, tree boxes, newsstands, and other designated fixtures. Plant and maintain flowers, trees, tree boxes, hanging flower baskets, and other landscaping around targeted GSA buildings. Operate a targeted rat abatement program wherever needed in the BID area. Homeless Services Engage a social services agency to provide full-time professional outreach workers to connect individuals experiencing homelessness with essential services, while helping GSA and other property owners eliminate encampments and aggressive panhandling. Coordinate efforts directly with the Department of Health (detox), Department of Mental Health (homeless outreach), Department of Employment Services, and Department of Human Services (food stamps and medical assistance) to deliver resources directly to the downtown homeless population. Focus on connecting the most entrenched population�specifically the severely mentally ill and those battling addictions�with housing recovery programs. Maintain and train a select group of Downtown Safety Ambassadors (SAM) to serve on the Homeless Outreach Service Team (HOST). Expand HOST activities to work with GSA, as well as public and private property managers, to discourage encampments and aggressive panhandling in private spaces. Coordinate outreach efforts with other Business Improvement Districts (BIDs). Develop additional strategies related to the 2nd and D Street shelter to improve the quality of life for GSA and other tenants in adjacent buildings. Expand the BID's education efforts to reach office workers, residents, and visitors. Economic Development Maintain its role as a center for research and information regarding the downtown economy Continue the collection and analysis of data, as well as the production of reports to help inform business and development decisions in the downtown area. Assist in developing financing plans and exploring possibilities for large-scale projects that support downtown infrastructure. General Support to GSA The BID�s professional staff and consultants will be facilitating collaborative planning with GSA and other major downtown stakeholders, including the city and private development community. This effort will address common concerns such as security, transportation and access, environmental issues, and development. The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition is 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1) as cited in FAR 6.302-1: �Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements�. Downtown BID is formally registered as a business improvement district in the District of Columbia and is the only firm capable of partnering with property owners in the designated area to provide a comprehensive bundle of enhanced services. These services go beyond the levels provided by other governmental or private sector sources. Currently, there is no other known public or private entity with the broad support and capacity required to simultaneously make the relevant area safe, clean, and user-friendly. The current contract is scheduled to expire on October 6, 2026. GSA will consider any bids, proposals, quotations, or capability statements. Any response shall be submitted via e-mail to Jose Nativisegovia, Contracting Officer via email at jose.nativisegovia@gsa.gov NO LATER THAN Tuesday, September 15, 2026 at 4:00 PM EST. The agency will consider any such submission.

title: Notice of Intent to Award Sole Source - Cold Weather Gear
description: THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS/QUOTES The 97th CON Squadron at Altus, OK 73523 intends to solicit and negotiate a sole-source, firm-fixed-price contract for the acquisition of cold weather gear. The 97th Contracting Squadron intends to make award this contract to AbilityOne San Antonio Lighthouse For The Blind (CAGE: 64083), under the AbilityOne Program. This acquisition is being conducted as a noncompetitive contract action under the authority of Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Overhaul (RFO) 6.103-5(b): "Authorized or required by statute". The AbilityOne Program dictates that the Lighthouse for the Blind is considered a Mandatory Source. The justification for soliciting and negotiating with a single source is as follows: AbilityOne Program Alignment: Fulfilling this order through the Lighthouse supports the federal policy of purchasing designated supplies and services from qualified nonprofit agencies employing people who are blind or severely disabled. This notice of intent is NOT a request for competitive proposals and no solicitation document exists for the requirement. Sources interested in responding to this notice are required to submit a capability statement that includes technical data and cost information, sufficient detail and with convincing evidence that clearly demonstrates the capability to meet the requirement. Requests for documentation, additional information, or submissions that only ask questions will not be considered as an affirmative response. A determination by the Government not to compete based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement or to proceed with a single source procurement. Capability statements are due on 09/18/26 by 10:00 AM CST. Capability statements shall be submitted by email ONLY as a Microsoft Word or Adobe PDF attachment to phillip.chambers.4@us.af.mil and ryan.lafever.2@us.af.mil. Capability statements and supporting documentation provided after the due date listed above will not be reviewed. Please see attached Single Source Justification for further information.

title: Monopole Tower Procurement and Base Foundation Construction (577 SWES/DIFF)
description: AMENDMENT #1 issued 3 September 2026, see attached documents. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items/services prepared in accordance with the format in FAR 12, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice and the attached Request for Quote (RFQ). The Government requires a contractor to provide all labor, materials, tools, equipment, transportation, and supervision necessary to procure, deliver, and install engineered foundations and complete 100-foot monopole towers at six (6) military installations nationwide. Locations of Work: McConnell Air Force Base, Kansas Goldwater Air National Guard Base, Arizona Fairchild Air Force Base, Washington Tinker Air Force Base, Oklahoma Grissom Air Reserve Base, Indiana Kirtland Air Force Base, New Mexico Key Scope Elements: Sourcing and delivery of certified 100-foot monopole towers to all locations. Conducting local geotechnical surveys and site engineering. Constructing reinforced concrete foundations designed for the towers. Erection and structural installation of the monopole towers. Installing associated grounding, lightning protection, and electrical infrastructure as detailed in the attached Statement of Work (SOW). Evaluation and Award This procurement is being conducted using Simplified Acquisition Procedures under FAR Part 13.5. Award will be made based on a simplified Best-Value Tradeoff. The Government will evaluate quotes based on: Technical Approach & Milestones (Assessed for clear understanding of the SOW, safety, and a realistic schedule) Past Performance (Two reference contacts for recent/relevant work) Price Site Visits Due to the geographic dispersion of the work sites, formal organized site visits may be limited. Offerors are highly encouraged to carefully review the SOW, site drawings, and FAR 52.236-3 (Site Investigation and Conditions Affecting the Work). To request a site visit at a specific location, please contact the Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist no later than 1 September 2026 at 1500Hrs EST. Submission Instructions Quotes must be submitted electronically via email. Please refer to the Addendum to FAR 52.212-1 (Instructions to Offerors) in the attached solicitation for detailed submission requirements. All questions regarding this solicitation must be submitted in writing via email by 7 September 2026 at 1500Hrs EST. Submit Quotes and Questions to: 101.msg.msc.contracting@us.af.mil

title: W912P626QA028 Mississinewa Lake Garage Door Replacement
description: **Notice ID:** W912P626QA028 **Primary Solicitation Manager:** Adam Haley **Subject:** Mississinewa Lake Garage Door Replacement **Description:** This Pre-Solicitation Notice is being issued by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Chicago District, to inform interested contractors of the District intent to issue a construction solicitation for the Mississinewa Lake Garage Door Replacement. **PROJECT INFORMATION:** This notice concerns a planned construction project for garage-door replacement and related facility improvements at Mississinewa Lake. **DESCRIPTION:** The project includes framing and enclosing open bays in the Old Barn and the lean-to on the New Barn; installing a metal ceiling; installing concrete footers, drainage, floors, and landings; performing asphalt removal, regrading, and resurfacing; adding or replacing exterior man doors, garage-door fixtures, overhead garage doors, and wall-mounted openers; and installing an industrial radio remote door and gate-opening system. The improvements are intended to provide secure and reliable access, improve drainage and weather protection, protect Government equipment, and extend the service life of the facilities. **CONTRACTING OFFICE:** U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Chicago District, 231 South LaSalle Street, Suite 1500, Chicago, IL 60604. **ACQUISITION INFORMATION:** The anticipated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 236220, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction, with a small-business size standard of $45 million. All responsible sources may submit a quotation, which will be considered by the Government. **OBTAINING TECHNICAL DATA:** Once the solicitation is posted, the solicitation, plans, specifications, and other technical documents will be available through the DoD Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) Solicitation Module. The solicitation will be downloadable from PIEE only. The project documents will be provided as PDF files that may be viewed, navigated, or printed using Adobe Acrobat Reader. Information regarding the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers process for settling requests for equitable adjustments and its duration goals for definitizing equitable adjustments arising from construction contract change orders is available at [https://www.usace.army.mil/Strategic-Partnerships/Partnering/mod/129895/details/443/](https://www.usace.army.mil/Strategic-Partnerships/Partnering/mod/129895/details/443/). After opening the page, scroll down the right side and select, View FFP Contract Changes Playbook Here. **IMPORTANT POLICY:** Contractors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) at the time their quotation is submitted to comply with annual representations and certifications requirements. Registration may be completed free of charge at [https://www.sam.gov](https://www.sam.gov). Contractors must register in SAM before registering in PIEE. Firms must also be registered in PIEE to access the solicitation and submit a quotation in response to the upcoming USACE solicitation. **POINT OF CONTACT:** The point of contact for this acquisition is Mr. Adam Haley at [adam.j.haley@usace.army.mil](mailto:adam.j.haley@usace.army.mil). Please include Notice ID W912P626QA028 on all correspondence.

title: U.S. Government Seeks to Lease Office and Related Space in Washington, DC
description: This is an amendment to the advertisement originally posted on May 28, 2026. This amendment has been issued to modify the additional requirements. Respondents to the initial advertisement do not need to respond to this modified advertisement. General Services Administration (GSA) seeks to lease the following space: State / State: Washington, DC Delineated Area: Washington, DC Central Employment Area (CEA) (See attached Map) Minimum Sq. Ft. (ABOA SF): 115,429 Maximum Sq. Ft. (ABOA SF): 121,200 Maximum Sq. Ft. (RSF): 138,515 Space Type: Office and related space Parking Spaces (Total): N/A Parking Spaces (Surface): N/A Parking Spaces (Structured): N/A Parking Spaces (Reserved): N/A Full Term: 20 Years Firm Term: 15 Years Option Term: N/A Additional Requirements: The offered building must have the ability to accommodate ISC Level III Security Requirements. (See FSL Level III requirements) The offered space must be contiguous, with the exception of the large-part breakdown space and the multipurpose space, both referenced below, provided all offered space meets the security requirements of the lease and is located within the offered building. The large-part breakdown space shall be approximately 3,330 ABOA SF with a minimum 11� 0� clear ceiling height. A portion of this large-part breakdown space, measuring approximately 60� long x 25� wide x 11� tall (clear ceiling height), shall be sufficient to accommodate a 2,000 lb. capacity bridge crane (measuring 42� long x 23� 6� wide x 10� tall) and shall have an 8� thick slab on grade or be capable of having suitable footings installed to meet structural engineering requirements for the crane. The offered building�s loading dock facilities shall be able to accommodate a crate with maximum dimensions of 50� wide x 80� tall x 96� long to be unloaded from a truck and delivered to the large-part breakdown space using a sit-down powered industrial truck. All spaces between the loading dock and the large-part breakdown space must have a minimum clear ceiling height of 7� 0�. The loading dock and the large-part breakdown space shall be within 300 feet of each other. The offered building must have a loading dock with a height of 42 inches, or have the capacity to adjust the height (e.g dock leveler) capable of accommodating a 26-foot box truck. The loading dock receiving area requires clear space adequate for a forklift turning radius and movement of crates with a dimension of 50� wide x 80� tall x 96� long (maximum). Approximately 17,818 ABOA SF of the space will be used as a laboratory. At least 6,000 ABOA SF of the laboratory space must have a floor rated to a 5,000 lb. concentrated load. The laboratory space shall have a minimum finished ceiling height of 8�3� clear. The path of travel from the loading dock to the laboratory must be able to accommodate crates with maximum dimensions of 48� wide x 80� tall x 50� long being maneuvered by pallet jack. If the path of travel includes a freight elevator, the elevator shall be within 300 feet of the laboratory and the loading dock and shall have a load capacity of at least 5,000 lbs. Approximately 11,600 ABOA SF of contiguous space will be designated as multipurpose space. Approximately 7,600 ABOA SF of this space shall be free of or have a limited number of columns to ensure the space can be designed with unobstructed sightlines. Not all minimum requirements are reflected in this advertisement. Offered space must meet all requirements outlined in this advertisement as well as comply with the performance standards set forth in the Lease which include but is not limited to requirements for fire safety and accessibility standards. A fully serviced lease is required. Offered space shall not be in the 1 percent-annual chance floodplain. Subleases will not be considered. Entities are advised to familiarize themselves with the telecommunications prohibitions outlined under Section 889 of the FY19 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), as implemented by the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR). For more information, visit: https://acquisition.gov/FAR-Case-2019-009/889_Part_B. Owners, brokers or agents may offer space for consideration. Any properties submitted by brokers or agents must be accompanied by written evidence that they are authorized by the ownership to exclusively represent the building offered. The General Services Administration (GSA) is using a tenant broker to represent the Government in this transaction. In no event shall a potential offeror enter into negotiations or discussions concerning a space to be leased with representatives of any federal agency other than the authorized offices and employees of the GSA or their authorized representative, CBRE, Inc. Expressions of interest should include the following information at a minimum: Building name, address, and age; Location of space in the building and date of availability; Rentable square feet (RSF) offered and rate per RSF; Name, address, telephone number, and email address of authorized contact; Information on building ownership. Expressions of Interest Due: September 15, 2026 Market Survey (Estimated): TBD Occupancy (Estimated): Winter 2028/2029 Send Expressions of Interest to: Name/Title: CBRE, Inc.
